input.summary:
Wing walkway is NOT lit: the walkway's air is owned by the mansion shell, so runParts refuses every lantern and chain placed there (all 12 floor cells stay at light 0). parts/room-25.mjs is unchanged (a no-op) and build.nbt is the current make.sh output with no walkway lights.
Measured in a scratch copy (lock ignored): two hanging lanterns at (49,15,66) and (49,15,71), chains at y16, light min 8 across all 12 cells. One lantern at z68 gives min 5 with 5 dim cells, so the designer's "one may be enough" is wrong.
Blocked on the shell's carve of x49 y11..16 z63..74; the lamplighter cannot clear it without touching the shell.
left: Walkway unlit: all 12 floor cells at light 0 (mobs spawn). The shell carves x49 y11..16 z63..74 as air and runParts locks it, so chains/lanterns at (49,15..16,66) and (49,15..16,71) are refused (confirmed: refusedAt lists all four, part 'room: wing walkway', refused 4).

Needs the shell owner to leave the chain and lantern cells (x49 y15..16 at z66 and z71) out of the carve or otherwise unlocked for a later part. Then this room part adds the two hanging lanterns (porch-style: iron_chain axis y at y16, lantern hanging true at y15). Measured: min 8, mean 9.5, 0 dim.
The room tool's suggested spot (49,11,67, a standing lantern on the floor) is in the one-wide lane and would cut the walk from z66 down to z68..74 (walkway reachability breaks). Do not use it.

The reading lectern at (49,11,74) that the designer mentioned is also refused by the same lock, so the dead-end reading point has no lectern in the current build either. This is the designer's and shell's call, not the lamplighter's.
The module parts/room-25.mjs is back to its original no-op after the probe; no lights are placed in the real build.

waste.what: Worked out lantern spacing cell by cell (light falls one per block, from y15 down to feet at y11) and then checked it by building scratch copies of the whole nbt, once with two lanterns and once with one.
waste.cost: about 6 tool calls and two full make-free scratch builds (node load/set/save plus mcd light); the answer is a single arithmetic rule: a lantern at y15 lights cells within 3 of it at light 8+.
waste.tool: mcd light (or room) with a what-if flag, e.g. `mcd light build.nbt --rooms rooms.json --try 49,15,66:lantern,49,15,71:lantern --only 'wing walkway'`, so a lamp layout is measured without a scratch copy or a rebuild.

waste.what: Tried placing the lanterns in the real build to see whether the shell lock refused them; had to edit room-25.mjs, run make.sh, read parts-report.json, then revert and rebuild.
waste.cost: 3 extra make.sh runs (about 1 minute each in this build), 2 edits.
waste.tool: A preflight in runParts or `mcd room` that lists the cells a part would be refused at ("lock: shell air at x49 y15..16 z66, z71") before the rebuild, or the room tool reporting lock status per room cell alongside the light map.

waste.what: Had to work out by hand which cells the shell's carve had locked and which were still writable: the walkway box and the walls around it.
waste.cost: one reading of room-25.mjs's header comment plus the parts-report refusedAt list.
waste.tool: `mcd plan` (or the room tool's floor grid) marking locked air as 'L' next to the furniture 'o', so a lock is seen without a build.

companions.task: re-cut the mansion shell's walkway carve (x49, z63..74, y11..16) so the chain and lantern cells at (49,15..16,66) and (49,15..16,71) stay unlocked for a later part; this is the shell owner's change, not the lamplighter's.
hang two lanterns from iron chains under the walkway ceiling at z66 and z71 (y15, chains at y16), and decide whether a reading lectern at (49,11,74) survives the lock.
